What you should do

Chapter 7

Result and Discussion

 

7.1 Performance Benchmarking

The main goal of this research is to identify the appropriate lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) for real-time offline mango variety classification on Android edge devices. While predictive accuracy remains an important performance indicator, deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained smartphones requires a broader evaluation that considers computational efficiency alongside classification performance. A model that achieves marginally higher accuracy may not necessarily be the most appropriate choice if it requires significantly larger storage, longer inference time, or greater computational resources. Therefore, this research adopts a comprehensive benchmarking methodology that evaluates multiple performance aspects before selecting the final deployment model.

 

To achieve an objective comparison, five transfer learning-based CNN architectures—MobileNetV2, MobileNetV3-Small, EfficientNetV2B0, DenseNet121, and NASNetMobile—were trained using the identical experimental configuration described in Chapter 3. Every architecture utilized the same Mangifera2012 dataset, identical preprocessing pipeline, online data augmentation strategy, training–validation split, optimizer configuration, batch size, learning rate, and early stopping criteria. Furthermore, all models employed the same custom classification head consisting of a Global Average Pooling layer, Dropout (0.30), a Dense layer with 128 neurons, and a Softmax output layer for the ten mango varieties. Maintaining identical training conditions ensures that differences observed during evaluation originate from the architectural characteristics of the CNN models rather than inconsistencies in the experimental setup.

Unlike conventional image classification studies that rely solely on overall accuracy, this research performs a deployment-oriented benchmarking analysis by evaluating both predictive and computational performance. Four classification metrics were used to measure recognition capability:

  • Classification Accuracy
  • Precision
  • Recall
  • Weighted F1-score

 

Since the final objective is mobile deployment, additional engineering metrics were also considered during benchmarking:

•       Model Storage Size (MB) – indicating the storage requirement of the trained model.

•       Inference Latency (ms) – representing the average prediction time required for a single image.

•       TensorFlow Lite Deployment Compatibility – evaluating the suitability of each architecture for Edge AI implementation.

By combining predictive performance with deployment efficiency , the benchmarking framework enables a balanced assessment of each CNN architecture

 

Evaluation Metrics

o   FN denotes False Negatives.

Recall measures the model's ability to correctly identify all samples belonging to a particular class:

The weighted F1-score combines precision and recall into a single performance measure while accounting for class imbalance:

These metrics collectively provide a more reliable assessment than accuracy alone, particularly for fine-grained image classification tasks where visually similar classes may lead to different types of classification errors.

7.2 Comparative Analysis

The experimental results indicate that EfficientNetV2B0 achieved the best classification performance, with 92.00% accuracy and the highest weighted F1-score. Its advanced feature extraction capability enabled effective discrimination of visually similar mango varieties. However, the larger model size and longer inference time limit its suitability for real-time deployment on resource-constrained mobile devices.

Among the lightweight models, MobileNetV3-Small achieved 88.5% accuracy, only 3.5% lower than EfficientNetV2B0. Despite this small performance gap, it offered the smallest model size and fastest inference speed, making it the most practical choice for Edge AI applications where storage, memory, and response time are critical.

DenseNet121 achieved 90.25% accuracy, demonstrating strong feature representation through dense connectivity. Nevertheless, its high storage requirement and slower inference reduce its effectiveness for smartphone-based deployment.

The baseline MobileNetV2 obtained 80.25% accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency through depthwise separable convolutions. However, the absence of architectural improvements such as squeeze-and-excitation modules and Hard-Swish activation resulted in lower recognition performance than MobileNetV3-Small.

NASNetMobile produced the lowest accuracy (81.75%) among the evaluated networks. Although generated through Neural Architecture Search, it failed to surpass MobileNetV3-Small and also required greater storage and inference time, making it less suitable for efficient edge deployment.

Overall, the comparison highlights that MobileNetV3-Small provides the most balanced trade-off between classification accuracy, computational efficiency, model size, and inference latency. These characteristics make it the most appropriate architecture for offline, real-time mango variety classification on Android-based edge devices.

7.3 Deployment-Oriented Model Selection

Selecting an Edge AI model requires balancing classification performance with deployment efficiency rather than focusing solely on accuracy. Although EfficientNetV2B0 achieved the highest accuracy, its larger model size, higher computational cost, and slower inference limit its practicality for offline mobile applications.

In contrast, MobileNetV3-Small delivered comparable recognition performance while requiring significantly fewer computational resources. Its compact architecture, low storage requirement, fast inference, and native compatibility with TensorFlow Lite make it well suited for Android-based edge devices used in agricultural environments.

Based on the overall benchmarking results, MobileNetV3-Small was selected as the deployment model for the proposed AmmChini AI system. The model was further optimized using TensorFlow Lite Float16 post-training quantization and integrated into the Flutter application to enable efficient, real-time offline mango variety classification.

7.2 Comparative Analysis

The benchmark results demonstrate that the evaluated CNN architectures exhibit different trade-offs between recognition performance and deployment efficiency. Although EfficientNetV2B0 achieved the highest classification accuracy and weighted F1-score, its larger model size and longer inference latency reduce its suitability for real-time deployment on resource-constrained Android devices.

Among the lightweight architectures, MobileNetV3-Small achieved competitive recognition performance while maintaining the smallest storage footprint and the fastest inference time. The relatively small reduction in accuracy compared with EfficientNetV2B0 is offset by substantial improvements in deployment efficiency, making it a practical choice for mobile Edge AI applications.

DenseNet121 also demonstrated strong classification capability but required considerably greater computational resources than MobileNetV3-Small. Similarly, MobileNetV2 provided efficient inference but achieved lower recognition performance than the newer lightweight architectures. NASNetMobile showed comparatively lower accuracy and offered no significant advantage in model size or inference speed.

Overall, the benchmark results indicate that MobileNetV3-Small provides the most effective balance between predictive performance and deployment efficiency, making it the most suitable architecture for offline Android-based mango variety classification.

7.3 Deployment-Oriented Model Selection

Model selection for Edge AI applications requires balancing recognition performance with computational efficiency rather than relying exclusively on classification accuracy. Although EfficientNetV2B0 achieved the highest predictive performance, its larger model size and slower inference reduce its practicality for deployment on smartphones with limited computational resources.

In contrast, MobileNetV3-Small achieved competitive recognition performance while requiring substantially less storage and providing faster inference. Its lightweight architecture and native compatibility with TensorFlow Lite make it well suited for offline image classification on Android devices.

Based on the overall benchmarking results, MobileNetV3-Small was selected as the deployment model for the proposed AmmChini AI system. The selected model was further optimized using TensorFlow Lite Float16 post-training quantization and integrated into the Flutter-based application, enabling real-time offline classification of Bangladeshi mango varieties.
